question.problem:
$$
|\begin{aligned}-6 & -3 & 13 & 13 \\ 1 & 1 & 2 & -4 \\ 3 & 1 & -2 & -5 \\ 19 & 2 & -7 & -5\end{aligned}|
$$

Consider the above $4\times 4$ determinant. Which of the following $3\times 3$ determinants has the same value?

*Hint: Use elementary row operations to make the entries above and below ${a}_{32}$ equal to zero.*
question.worked_solution:
Let's make entries above and below ${a}_{32}=1$ equal to zero using elementary row operations.

Since adding a multiple of one row (or column) to another row (column) in a matrix does not change the value of its determinant, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}-6 & -3 & 13 & 13 \\ 1 & 1 & 2 & -4 \\ 3 & 1 & -2 & -5 \\ 19 & 2 & -7 & -5\end{aligned}| &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+3{R}_{3} \\ {R}_{2}:={R}_{2}-{R}_{3} \\ {R}_{4}:={R}_{4}+(-2){R}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & =|\begin{aligned}3 & 0 & 7 & -2 \\ -2 & 0 & 4 & 1 \\ 3 & 1 & -2 & -5 \\ 13 & 0 & -3 & 5\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the result along the $2$nd column, we get

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}3 & 0 & 7 & -2 \\ -2 & 0 & 4 & 1 \\ 3 & 1 & -2 & -5 \\ 13 & 0 & -3 & 5\end{aligned}| \\  & =1\cdot (-1)^{3+2}|\begin{aligned}3 & 7 & -2 \\ -2 & 4 & 1 \\ 13 & -3 & 5\end{aligned}| \\  & =-|\begin{aligned}3 & 7 & -2 \\ -2 & 4 & 1 \\ 13 & -3 & 5\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$
